reviews.text: Jinli Ancient Street is lively and vibrant, especially in the evening when the lanterns light up. Perfect for a leisurely walk and photos. There are many Sichuan street snacks and local foods along the street. The variety is good. Some snacks are tasty, others are just average, so it’s better to try small portions. It does get quite crowded, but it’s still enjoyable for strolling and soaking in the ambience. Worth visiting for the experience and atmosphere when you’re in Chengdu.

Paired with Wuhouci, this is a definitive stop in Chengdu. It is undeniably touristy, but a visit here still feels necessary. The architecture alone is worth the trip. We were captivated by the "old-world" preservation—the picturesque pedestrian lanes, wooden steles, and ornate pagodas genuinely evoke the Three Kingdoms era. The atmosphere manages to be passionate yet composed, with a bustling energy that feels authentic despite the commercial elements. A heads up: * The narrow lanes can get "shoulder-to-shoulder" crowded. Come early to beat the rush, it is the best way to appreciate the craftsmen and the architectural details in peace. * Very commercialize and touristy That said, worth the visit for the atmosphere and the snacks, together with the visit to Wuhouci (Wuhou Shrine).

Jinli Ancient Street is a great place to experience Chengdu’s traditional culture and local street food. The atmosphere is lively, especially in the evening when the red lanterns are lit. There are many local snacks, souvenirs, and small shops to explore. It can get quite crowded. On a rainy day, walking with an umbrella may feel a little inconvenient, but it brings a different charm — a reminder that not every journey is smooth, yet it still has its own beauty. Best visited at night.
Very clean and chill place. I really enjoy walking on these streets. There are many gift shops, you can buy variety of cute souvenirs here. Even the public toilet is very clean! Well maintained 👍

A vibrant and lively ancient street that captures the essence of traditional Chengdu through its well-preserved architecture and bustling market stalls that offers local snacks, signature foods, and local made souvenirs.

It's all tourist traps. Super crowded. Just overpriced souvenir shops. The food that's available is expensive, and there's nothing you can't get for cheaper from the surrounding area. The historic buildings itself should be nice, except you'll not get to see much of it because the entire area is buried under/hidden behind colourful shop fronts, poorly made-up tacky photo spots, bright lights, and loud music.

Jinli is a famous ancient street in Chengdu, Sichuan province. It is known for its beautiful Qing Dynasty-style architecture and stunning red lanterns, creating a lively and vibrant atmosphere, especially in the evening. The street is lined with shops selling souvenirs and handicrafts, and most importantly, it offers a wide variety of local food and snacks to try. It's a great spot for tourists to experience authentic Sichuan culture and cuisine.

There's not much to do here. Many other ancient town that's more interesting. This place is rather small. Street food & snacks quite limited & doesn't taste good. Watched a 30-minute cultural performance here. The show & place is pretty lacking. At other streets, u can get it cheaper with a better stage.
Nice during the day, more beautiful during the night. A lot of shops for tourists, a block of streets frozen in the time.
If you like Chinese history particularly in The Three Kingdoms also dining local Chinese food and beverage so this street is clicked for your lifestyle I do believe.

An awesome experience walking through the beautiful alleys. A bit overly commercialized but that's what always happens. Loads of interesting food options to choose from. You find most of the same food choices on the kuan zhai alleys too. Fun and interesting for kids - can rent a stroller across the main street.
A great place to wander around after dinner. And try out those local delicacies... Also located close to 武侯祠👍
A nice place to stroll around since there are a lot of stalls, shops, and sights to see. There are also a lot of food stalls and vendors selling souvenirs. I’d highly recommend tourists to visit.
A tourist walking street which looks good with the lights on in the evening but nothing extraordinary about the shops in the area.

Visited Jinli Ancient Street (锦里) on a weekday morning. The crowd was minimal and most shops had just opened, making it a relaxing stroll. While the street has charm and traditional architecture, many of the stores sell similar souvenirs and snacks. It took us about 1.5 hours to explore the entire area at a comfortable pace. If you are short on time, this spot can be skipped — but if you have a bit more flexibility in your itinerary, it is still worth a visit to soak in the old Chengdu vibes.
So beautiful!!! Love this place so much and the weather was amazing in December as well

Jinli Ancient Street (锦里古街) in Chengdu is a captivating blend of history, culture, and vibrant street life. Nestled in the Wuhou District, right next to the famous Wuhou Temple, it’s often called the “First Street of the Shu Kingdom” due to its origins dating back over 1,800 years43dcd9a7-70db-4a1f-b0ae-981daa162054. 🌸 What Makes Jinli Special - Architecture: Traditional Qing Dynasty-style buildings with curved roofs, wooden facades, and red lanterns line the stone-paved alleys. - Street Food Paradise: Try spicy tofu, Dan Dan noodles, sweet rice balls, and even grilled rabbit head if you're feeling adventurous. - Cultural Performances: Enjoy Sichuan Opera, especially the mesmerizing face-changing act, often performed in open-air tea houses. - Handicrafts & Souvenirs: From Shu embroidery to shadow puppets and calligraphy, it’s a treasure trove for art lovers like you. - Atmosphere: At night, the lantern-lit streets create a magical, almost cinematic vibe—perfect for photography. Given your love for visual aesthetics and photography, Chanat, Jinli would be a dream to capture—especially during golden hour or when the lanterns glow after sunset. Would you like tips on the best photo spots or how to plan a visit?
A popular tourist historical place (relating to romanance of the 3 kingdom) with plenty of shops, eatery and public toilets.

Visiting this place during the day and night offers two completely different experiences. I came here twice once during the day to soak in the vibrant local culture, and again at night when the lanterns light up, creating a magical atmosphere. Unlike Kuan Zhai Alley’s modern, laid-back vibe, this place is vibrant and brimming with old-world charm. It feels like stepping into a Sichuan fairy tale!

Popular tourist street with lots of street food and ancient China vibes. Good for a walk around and picture taking session. Food prices are higher than in non tourist areas, but can be worth trying bits and pieces.
Must see in China. Not only because of Pandas, not only because of spice food, but because THIS IS CHENGDU !!!
Torusit attraction of a cultural and historical district furnished into a night market full of local snacks and shows. Average size area easy to walk around and not get lost.

Jin Li Ancient Street, like Kuanzhai Alley, has many shops and food options inside. But what we like about Jin Li is that the options seem to be much more affordable. Instead of Starbucks at Kuanzhai Alley, you find the local brand Mixue here. This time, we tried the Green Tea with Milk (6RMB – $1.5) which was refreshing. The Beef Guo Kui (锅盔) or a fried flat bread with fillings was 15 RMB for the beef version. Delicious but we were to try the more delectable one a few days later back in Chengdu. Also, we enjoyed the stroll here a little more because it was an easy walk – just all the way down and loop back the same way. A little bridge that crossed a little stream at the end is a signal to show that you should turn back right about there. For more details, visit 2bearbear today!

Great Place to walk around to see all the old maintain buildings around Chengdu... Some are rebuild but some are really old... There's lots of restaurants n stores around...n many nice spots to take nice pictures.. Is very crowded even on weekdays...so cannot imagine how crowded will it be on weekends n holidays...

Very popular tourist attraction next to the Wuhou shrine. It’s very pretty at night with all the lanterns lit up. It’s really fun to stroll through with so many different food vendors and little shops.

No entrance fees are needed. This is one straight line shopping street. Therefore, there are 2 entrance points. We entered at the entrance near wu hou chi. Almost same as kuanzhai xiangzi (wide street narrow street). Many eatery stalls here. There are 2 stalls that caught my attention. First, I particularly liked the "ye popo bongbong ji" (skew food with meat or vege in a stick). Second, sandapao (3 big cannons), a sweet delicacy. There are so many photo spots here.

"Jinli"..an ancient village now turned into commercialised tourist attractions with lots of food and local crafts on sale. Its an interesting place to visit..walk along the many alleyways passing by cafes & shops and even a Starbucks!! Its very crowded on most days even on an offpeak season filled with local tourists. You can find face changing performances here, standup comedy Chinese-style of course, mini opera shows which gives you a glimpse of the olden day cultures.

I was starving when I ate here so anything would have sufficed. Got some Sichuan flavoured tofu and some bread with brown sugar inside. It defo needed more sugar. Also it's really hard to eat soft tofu with a toothpick. I was using more energy trying to eat it than the energy I was getting from eating it.

Jinli Pedestrian Street, located east of Chengdu's Wuhou Memorial Temple, is known as "the first street of the Shu Kingdom". This place is also praised as Chengdu's "Riverside Scenery at the Ming Festival", making visitors feel like they have returned to the distant Three Kingdoms period, more than 1800 years ago. A special and not-to-be-missed feature at Cam Ly Walking Street is the rich menu with a variety of Chengdu's specialty dishes and snacks. If you are a food lover, this is heaven for you. Spicy or sweet, crunchy or soft, you can always find your favorite dish here when traveling to China. The local dishes on Cam Ly Walking Street are rich in local flavor and very reasonable prices. The only thing you need to keep in mind is to come on an empty stomach so you can try all the delicious dishes here.

Old street brimming with Chinese heritage and culture. The best to visit in nightfall with the narrow streets lit with red lanterns really increases the vibes by ten folds. It’s a place to get bites and souvenirs - but I wouldn’t recommend as some tend to be more expensive than other locations. Overall a must visit when in Chengdu!

Old city vibes. A must visit for travellers to Chengdu. Be sure to visit 武侯祠 right next to the old shopping street. Took a star off because there were just too many touts. Marred the experience a little.

Jinli is connected to wu hou shrine so after our visit in the park, we walked over. There’s a lot of beer and tea shops as well as stalls selling food. Lots of spicy food too. Tell the stall owner if u don’t want or less spicy food. Love the rustic feel of the place. Be careful when you walk so not to fall into the ditch, no railings! I bought some nougat at Kuan zai lane and found that it’s cheaper in jinli.
Very nice place, a bit crowded but understandable ☺️ many tasty street food and excellent tea (also gorgeous barista) love craftsmanship that still exists here

This place has commercialization that overwhelms culture and traditions. It’s crowded with many businesses. The real culture were buried under the noise and lights. However, still an interesting place to visit. The food was not great. Not authentic.
We're there on a Friday night. this little area is fully packed with locals and tourists. only street food available in this place and recommended to have full meal in other area.
A touristy road in Chengdu with a lot of souvenir shops and fast food stands. Don't come here if you are looking for proper healthy food. Beside roaming around there is not much to do.
Nice, unique, pedestrianized place. Location adjacent to Chengdu Wu Hou Shrine Lots of souvenir and food vendors. Unfortunately, there are still not many that provide halal food signs for Muslims.

Super touristic but a must go the first time here! Got recommended to come here by other guests in my hostel, you can find many vendors selling traditional food and the price is a bit pricey compare to other local alley. You can also see the show of famous face changing in chengdu here!
Fun place to wander around and see another historic pedestrian walking area near the temple next door. Loads of shops to buy fun local goods, and there are plenty of food options. Highly recommend!
Wow! U can literally spend a day here! A lot to see n shop n eat! A must visit place when u come to Chengdu!

Old streets of Chengdu replica building structure with modern facilities Hand Craft center with arts, handmade, local souvenirs shops many places to eat Snacks, full meal, steamboats, desserts or fritters

A must-go place in Chengdu. It's one of those places where you will see modernity meets tradition and west meets east. Inside this commercialized 'village', you will see ancient Chinese architecture everywhere. Most houses have now been transformed into shops and restaurants. While many sell traditional Chinese delicacies and various souvenirs, there are also western restaurants and cafes. The village has a festive atmosphere. You may occasionally hear people singing live inside some cafes or in some open space. Most alleys in the village are packed with visitors. If you want to get out of the crowd for some fresh air, you may go to the pond somewhat in the middle of the village where you may take a seat at some eateries there for some refreshment and enjoy the beautiful view of the pond and the bridges.
Nice place but for the Temple inside you need to buy a ticket and they needed my passport 😂😂😂 so no.... I didn't go in.
I liked this more than the kwanzai alley. This place was super crowded with many little lanes selling street food, crafts etc. Very lively and a little overwhelming at times.
Great tourist attraction to visit, but very crowded at most times throughout the day.
Visited the place after most of the stores have closed. Even though it was rather deserted by the time I was there, it offered an opportunity out for some quiet photography opportunity.
Ancient touristy street with plenty of modern stalls for food and gifts. Nice tourist spot, good strolling location.

A pedestrian street in old-style construction, but not really old, with shopping and eateries. Since it is right next to the Wu Hou Shrine people will naturally walk it through on the way. Street shops are not particularly expensive but eating here can be about double of that outside.
Chinese old building and culture with yummy local food. Should visit when come to Chengdu

There is no entrance fee; it’s just an open walking street with strict prohibition of any vehicles two or four wheelers. The 550 m street consists of gifts shops & small food stalls also that have a variety of unseen food delicacies which are really very spicy.

(Also known as Jin-Li) high traffic, tourists spot. Moment you walk in, your heart does sink as you'll see a giant Starbucks filled with local visitors. Walk a bit further in, you'll come across a StreetFood Market, where some food would be great, whilst some wouldn't be. Ensure you find out which is which, spicy or not before you buy.
- Smaller but somehow feels more crowded than Kuan Zhai Alley. - Similar to Kuan Zhai Alley. Even sells similar stuffs.

Wow, this place is absolutely amazing! It's like stepping back in time, all the way to 1000 years ago when China was down to earth and filled with friendly people. You won't believe the surprises and mesmerizing sights that await you here. Everywhere you look, there are incredible art stores showcasing traditional food and crafts. And if you're in the mood for some fun, there are plenty of bars with lively live music. Trust me, you're going to love it here!
beautiful place, good to go late afternoon to enjoy the day and the night of the place..

This is a very crowded street with lots of shops selling little fun stuff and also food. There are many stalls to choose from and the variety is interesting. If you are going there, consider visiting the the other three place which are just next to it. The place is closely related to the famous novel, Romance of the Three Kingdoms, so there are many shops selling things from that novel. Many shops do not have seating so you are expected to eat while standing or walking like the locals. Great place for people watching but not for those who hate crowd.
This is the very place where crowded too much. I couldn't do and see anything but peoples in here.

This is a very popular old street with well preserved ancient houses that attracts both locals and tourist alike. It is quite big place and took us about 2-3 hours to walk through the crowded alleys and stop by a restaurant for lunch. Don't miss out the food street on the left once you enter the main gate. You can find all kinds of Chengdu food include rabbit heads, pig nose etc.
Cultural old architecture. Lots of delicious street food & immense yourself in its cultural vibes

I spent an evening wandering around here. I didn’t feel very spendy, but if I had, there would have been a lot of fun, touristy things to buy, and lots of different foods to try. On a busy night, the whole place feels atmospheric and festive. I liked knowing that although the place felt commercial, it had already been commercial for hundreds of years.

One of a must see tourist spots, this ancient chinese walking street is very lively and intersting. This place is good for window shopping or buying some souvenir or even just walking around. There are also serveral restaurants (kind of bar style) that you could enjoy live music and drink or just a regular restaurant for dinner.
Went there late around 10pm, all stores are closing, good looking red latente along the street.
Even though it was a weekday, it was very crowded. It's difficult to find toilet.

I love this place where public WiFi is provided. Very convenient! Basically it is a small shopping street, somehow like 南锣鼓巷 in Beijing. People can do a little shopping outside of 武侯祠, which is next to 锦里. You can find souvenirs there.

One of the tourists spot area in Chengdu. It's more well known as Jinli Street. Lined with stores to get your gifts and local foods. Make sure to try it during night time as an alternative. As it gets much better to take your pictures too.
The most representative place in Chengdu, it combines food and culture. The architectural type is particularly unique, with both ancient and modern coexisting.

Though maybe somewhat a tourist trap, but it has many interesting shops and restaurants. As compared to other similar places, this place is worth visiting, walking around, eating some local food, browsing thru many little interesting shops!

It's so popular among locals and tourists for food and shipping (for very good reasons) that the cultural aspect is no doubt diluted. Worth visiting if you travel to Chengdu but be reminded of the crazy crowd.
Best place in town for local snacks. Bought some spicy rabbit and lamb meat here. Cool ancient architecture.
Get a local guide as it's good to understand the significance to China of this place . Well worth a visit
Many street vendors, neat and clean (relatively). Red lanterns are displayed along the road.
Interesting for foreigner but to the local its a place for tea ..local snacks ( taste are not very nice ..some too spicy and too sweet ) and some beer..over all nice place to buy some souvenirs.
Interesting place for a walk during the day and in the evening. Its very crowded tho, a lot of strong smells from the street foods.
Tourist attraction. That's it! Attracts tourists with its novelty but that's it! Nice place for photos but crowded.
Many snacks(^o^) And every Chinese new year, Lantern Festival will be held here.
I would not say it is very good, that why I give it three. You can hardly get into the feeling of ancient China culture. Too many people, High price.
Jinli Street - The Street of Embroidery Workshops - The Paradise of Chengdu and Sichuan Opera
李山山锦里 staff are very nice and offer good service. The drink tastes good as well ;) highly recommend you to visit🙊💗💗

I visited Li Shan Shan Café in Chengdu, and it was such a charming and aesthetic place. The atmosphere felt calm and cozy, perfect for relaxing or taking photos. The drinks were beautifully presented and tasted great, and the staff were friendly and welcoming. Definitely a must-visit spot if you’re in Chengdu.

中国の老街巡りが好きで、成都では都江堰古鎮と錦里に行ってみました☺︎錦里は成都で一番有名な古街で、1800年もの歴史があります(三国時代)。入場無料で、入り口に錦里と書いてあるので迷わないかと思います。リノベーションされており凄く綺麗で、ほぼ真っ直ぐの一本道に飲食店、お土産やさん、文化体験などがぎゅっと詰まっていました。距離は550mほど。疲れず迷わずまわりやすい。夜は提灯が灯され映え映えに。 すぐ横には三国志ゆかりのスポット武侯祠博物館がありました。武侯祠と錦里両方行くと半日は楽しめます♪

とても楽しかった 「錦里（ジンリー）」は、中国・四川省成都市にある人気の観光スポットです。 ​主に以下のような特徴があります。 ​歴史的な街並みの再現: 明や清の時代の建築様式を再現した古い街並みが魅力です。三国志の雰囲気が漂う古風な通りとして知られています。 ​「武候祠」に隣接: 成都の有名な観光地である「武候祠（三国時代の蜀漢の丞相、諸葛亮らを祀る場所）」に隣接しており、一体として観光できます。 ​四川の文化とグルメ: ​四川省ならではの**軽食（小吃）**のお店が数多く並び、食べ歩きが楽しめます（例：担担麺、鉢鉢鶏、麻辣兔頭など）。 ​四川独特の**川劇（せんげき）**など、文化的なパフォーマンスを鑑賞できる場所もあります。 ​夜景: 夕暮れ時になると提灯（赤い灯籠）に明かりが灯り、レトロでロマンチックな雰囲気に包まれるため、特に夜の散策がおすすめです。 ​お土産: 地元の手工芸品や、パンダ柄などのユニークなお土産屋も豊富にあります。 ​中国の古い歴史と文化、そして活気ある成都の庶民の生活文化を感じられる場所です。

Jinli Old Street เป็นถนนเก่าแนวสถาปัตยกรรมเสฉวนที่คึกคักที่สุดในเฉิงตู เต็มไปด้วยร้านของกินท้องถิ่น ขนมพื้นเมือง ของฝาก งานหัตถกรรม และคาเฟ่สวย ๆ บรรยากาศยามค่ำจะเด่นเป็นพิเศษเพราะโคมแดงทั้งถนน ทำให้ได้ฟีลจีนโบราณแบบมีชีวิต เหมาะทั้งเดินเล่น ถ่ายรูป และล่าอาหารสตรีทฟู้ดในที่เดียว
三国聖地にやってまいりました。 ここではお土産に張飛牛肉を買って帰りました。 張飛牛肉って何？ たぶん張飛のイメージだろうと思ってこれは買わねばとお買い上げしました。 家に帰って食べると、まあ普通のジャーキーでしたね。 ちょっと期待値が高めだったので少しテンション、下がり目でした。
Jinli ancient street, Instagramable, hanya kurang cocok dgn street food nya yg rata2 rasa pedas mala (kebas khas chongqing)

La Calle Jinli es una antigua calle de 1800 años de antigüedad en Chengdu, famosa por su arquitectura tradicional china, artesanías locales, comida callejera y ambiente vibrante. Es un destino turístico muy popular que atrae a multitudes (fundamentalmente chinas) y ofrece una mezcla de elementos históricos y modernos, incluyendo tiendas y arte popular.
吃完饭来锦里旅游一哈 原来住到这边的时候经常来 现在都很难有机会过来了 走到武侯祠大街上清风雅静的 想到锦里应该莫得好多人 结果走到门口一哈就感受到著名景区的闹热了 天那么冷过来耍的还真不少 一路拉通各种吃事 一样试吃一哈走一半路就可以吃饱 这次来比几年前来规模又扩大了 打造得相当不错 在全国的古镇里面绝对是出类拔萃的
原本的古建築被破壞後, 這些年搭配復古風而重新打造仿古式的建築群, 成都地鐵10號線武候祠站可到. 清一色是賣吃的跟記念品的風景區, 價格也較貴, 過度商業化了. 秋天有銀杏黃葉可以拍. 這市區景點人多, 也吸引攝影同好來拍照.
20251024錦里，又名錦里一條街、錦里古街，是位於中國四川省成都市的一條古商業街，最早可追溯到秦漢時期。傳說中錦里曾是西蜀歷史上最古老、最具有商業氣息的街道之一，早在秦漢、三國時期便聞名全國。錦里毗鄰武侯祠，頗有古蜀國民風。現在的錦里已經被開發成一條民俗商業步行街，混合三國文化以及川西文化。 感覺沒以前繁華~很多商家都收起來了
무후사 옆에 위치한 Old Street 입니다. 청두가 비단으로 유명한 도시여서, 비단을 뜻하는 금锦으로 이름 붙였다 하네요. 솔직히 어디에나 있는, 별다른 특색없는 그런 거리 입니다. 무후사 관람 후에 잠깐 둘러보는 정도면 족해 보이네요.
Chunxi Road. ถนนโบราณจินหลี่ (Jinli Ancient Street / 锦里古街) แหล่งรวมวัฒนธรรมโบราณ ถนนคนเดินที่สวยงาม มีของขายหลากหลาย ถ่ายรูปสวย

Molto suggestivo di sera, con le lanterne accese. Bello perdersi per le varie vie curiosando tra i vari negozi. Interessante il gelato verde al gusto macha. E possibile vedere anche degli antichi varchi tornando dal centro dei mercati verso l'uscita a sud ovest

phố cổ Cẩm Lý tuyệt đẹp và có nhiều gian hàng đồ lưu niệm, quán ăn (đậu phụ thúi) và rất nhiều quán trà sữa (như Chagee, starbuck,...) phù hợp với khẩu vị của khách du lịch nước ngoài như mình - 锦里古街/Jinli gu jie is beautiful and has many souvenir stalls, food stalls (stinky tofu) and many milk tea shops (like Chagee, Starbuck,...) suitable for the taste of foreign tourists like me.
Bellissimo quartiere con un fascino retrò, negozietti e street food. Cercate su AMap Jinli Old Street (Main Gate).
時間が沢山あればぶらぶら楽しい場所です。 お土産屋など沢山集まっています。 お茶屋さんが扇風機を使って、良い茶葉の香りを飛ばしてきたのには釣られて買いたくなりました！
Очень красивая аутентичная улица со старыми строениями, необычным декором и элементами. Можно продегустировать, а также приобрести чай или различные угощения.
Byliśmy tam wieczorem, bo to bardzo ładne zabytkowe uliczki blisko dużego parku. Wieczorem można kupić pamiątki, rękodzieło oraz jakieś bibeloty. Jest tam dużo restauracji z dobrym jedzeniem.
緊臨武侯祠的錦里古街，週六的下午人潮不算多，可能有點飄雨關係，這裏的歷史古蹟古色古香，不像其他古街較商業化及過度改建。夜晚的錦里比白天更美，建議下午來逛品嚐美食。這裏物價比其他區稍貴，若要購買伴手禮或紀念品，可以再多比較一下價格喔。

從高升橋站地鐵C出口，錦里與武侯祠僅一墻之隔，不管是先去哪兒，魚水互幫的結果就是人滿為患，另外就是體力與腳勁的考驗，二個地方參觀加上餐飲的時間，保守估計最少要4-6小時才夠用，必要的心裏與身體準備，是來此一遊的功課。 這次來四川也將近十天，從成都吃到樂山，又從樂山吃回成都，連青城山的齋飯都吃光光，川式小吃與餐飲幾乎都已經嘗試一輪，錦里的美食與其他景點相比，其實大同小異差別不大，只要不怕麻辣對味覺的衝擊，就能好好享受，要被打槍的機會不大，所以大可放膽一試。

Altra tappa imperdibile di chengdu. La zona vecchia della città pullula di vita e di bancarelle. Qui lo shopping è interessante ed i ritirati non mancano. I prezzi sono sempre buoni ed il cibo mediamente economico. Ci sono diverse aree dove i locali si ritrovano e si conoscono e dove si può bere un ottimo tè. Spesso troverete rappresentazioni teatrali o musicali. Fermati a bere un the!

สถานที่แห่งนี้เป็นซอยข้างวัดที่มีกิจกรรมต่างๆให้เราได้ทำรวมถึงมีร้านค้าร้านขายของกินของใช้ต่างๆของที่ระลึกรวมถึงแสดงถึงประวัติศาสตร์ของความเป็นวัดแห่งนี้และมีที่ปราจีนบุรีใจก็คือจะเป็นที่แคะหู หากใครต้องการที่จะมาแคะหูที่นี่รับรองไม่ผิดหวัง สะใจมากๆเลย

Eine sehr schöne Tagesreise. Sehr viele kleine Shops sehr viele gute Leckereien. Hier kann man Kungfu Tee trinken das ist ein echtes Erlebnis und dein Mann mit 1000 Gesichtern echt coole Show gibt’s in fast jeden Teehaus dort.

เมืองโบราณ จัดวางทุกอย่างได้อย่างลงตัว บ้านไม้โบราณที่โอบล้อมสายน้ำไว้ ตกแต่งแสงสีไว้อย่างสวยงาม เพื่อล่อหลอกให้นักท่องเที่ยวเข้ามาเยี่ยมยาม แนะนำให้มาเดินช่วงเย็นๆ ถึงค่ำ เพราะจะมีการแสดงบนเวทีกลางน้ำ แสง สี เสียง ชนะเลิศ มีร้านอาหารหลากหลายให้ได้นั่งดื่มกินกัน อาหารแบบสตรีทฟู๊ดก็มากมาย
好吃好買也好逛的園區，裡面大大小小的商家，很有意思的大型藝文美食區，濃濃的中式風情，很多具有特色的建築，還有各種成都美食。 園區很大，光是逛滿一圈就會眼花撩亂，可以找個茶樓坐一會兒，看個劇喝茶聊天，十分愜意。
Esta zona es de visita obligada en Chengdu, hay una amplia variedad de puestos de comida y bebida y de souvenirs de pandas 🐼Es muy muy bonito y es agradable ir por sus calles.
来成都之必游之地址- ，锦里古街。另一个让人在成都留连忘返的必游之地。隔邻就是武候祠三囯文化中心，想了解多些三囯历史的，可先到武候祠，然后再走来连接隔邻的锦里古镇。 来过数次，每次都很喜欢。两旁旧屋很有情调，小桥小溪等，还有很多美食，手信，记念品等。可以走个半天以上。
Phố ban ngày lãng mạn, ban đêm lên đèn rất đẹp nhưng rất đông đúc. Bên trong là cửa hàng bán các sản phẩm và các hàng quán ăn uống
武侯祠の隣。 街並みや夜景がとても綺麗で、昼も夜もお勧め。 土産物屋、食堂、耳掃除、スタバ、切り絵、三国志ショーなど、様々な店があり、いつも大勢の客で賑わっている。 錦里が好きすぎて、2週間の滞在中5〜6回ここに行った。 入口近くにはmobikeのレンタル自転車置場とバス停がある。 錦里と杜甫記念館は直通バスがあるらしい。 確か50or60元。

“ศาลเจ้าสามก๊ก” Chengdu Wu Hou Shrine แห่งเมืองเฉิงตู เมืองที่มีประวัติศาสตร์ยาวนานนับพันๆ ปี บันทึกเรื่องราวเกิดขึ้นในปลายสมัยของราชวงศ์ฮั่นตะวันออกของจักรพรรดิเหี้ยนเต้ เนื่องจากในสมัยนั้นเล่าปี่ตั้งราชธานีที่เสฉวนโดยมีขงเบ้งมาช่วยเล่าปี่บริหาร มีทหารเอกคือกวนอู เตียวหุย ซึ่งเป็นพี่น้องร่วมสาบานกัน ประชาชนในเมืองเสฉวนต่างก็มีความสุข แต่เมื่อสิ้นบุญของเล่าปี่แล้วประชาชนกลับนับถือขงเบ้ง (จูกัดเหลียง) มากกว่าเล่าปี่ ประชาชนก็เลยสร้างศาลเจ้าขึ้นมาเพื่อระลึกถึง ต่อมาไม่นานผู้ปกครองเมืองจีนเห็นว่าไม่ถูกต้องที่ยกย่องขุนนางให้อยู่เหนือกษัตริย์ก็เลยออกคำสั่งให้ สร้างศาลเล่าปี่โดยให้มีรูปปั้นขุนนางอีก 14 ท่าน เอาไว้ด้วย

清末、民初保留下來的一條街道。街道兩旁留下不少古舊的建築物，當然著名的景點免不了滲透着商業的味道。但細心欣賞可以品味一下川蜀的飲食文化，建築風格，當地的風土人情。整體感覺不錯。

锦里是展示三国文化的仿古商业街，也是成都武侯祠博物馆的一部分，是成都人气最旺景点之一。传说，锦里曾是西蜀历史上最古老、最具有商业气息的街道之一，早在秦汉、三国时期便闻名全国，其历史可以追溯到1800多年前。古街里青瓦错落有致，青石板路蜿蜒前行，建筑古色古香，仿佛回到当年的天府市井，一进去就能看到两遍店铺挂的红灯笼，，所以晚上去夜晚的锦里，亮起了大红灯笼就便仿佛现出锦城真正的模样来的一种感觉。夜晚的锦里，人丝毫没有减少，反而有增加的趋势。在这条街上，浓缩了成都生活的精华：有茶楼、客栈、酒楼、酒吧、戏台、风味小吃、工艺品、土特产，充分展现了三国文化和四川民风民俗的独特魅力。
錦里古街離地鐵站有段距離，回程時搭了電動三輪車到高升橋地鐵站（費用12），假日就是人多，感覺就是人擠人，看了不少大陸內地人，比較有意思的是讓女兒吹了一個糖老鼠（師傅問生肖），光過程就很有意思了！費用38

삼국지의 유비,관우,장비의 촉나라 였던 진리.(중국식 발음. 택시 탈 때 참고하세요.) 그 촉나라 거리를 재현한 중국스러운 거리. 사천 지방 특유의 매운 먹거리가 많이 팔고 있고 기념품도 많이 파는데 콴자이 샹즈 지역보다 이곳이 퀄리티도 좋고 가격이 더 저렴하다. 여행 추천 시간은 늦은 오후에가서 무후사를 보고 해가 지면서 진리거리를 돌며 식사 및 쇼핑을 추천합니다.

Vũ Hầu Tự, 1 di tích lịch sử liên quan đến thời Tam Quốc của vùng đất Thành Đô thủ phủ của nước Ba Thục, nơi thờ Khổng Minh và các đệ tử của ông, cũng là nơi có mộ của Lưu Bị (mộ gió?) Cạnh bên là phố đi bộ Cẩm Lý cũng là một điểm tham quan thu hút khách du lịch khi đến Thành Đô Tứ Xuyên.

Vale la penta perderse por sus calles que bordean el parque del templo y por todos sus locales. La ubicacion es la entrada a este conjunto de calles. Cuenta con muchos locales de comida callejera, pero tambien restaurantes y tiendas de regalos diversas. Tiene muchisimo ambiente local, y por la noche esta precioso iluminado. A partir de la tarde muchos locales cuentan con musica en directo, y tambien en alguna plaza.

ถนนคนเดินบรรยากาศเมืองโบราณ ร้านค้ามากมาย Starbuck อาหารท้องถิ่น ชา โมเดล พู่กัน ของเล่น ขนม ขนมโบราณ ชุด cosplay จีนโบราณ ถ้าจะให้เดินทั่วน่าจะมี 3 ชม. ขึ้นไป บางร้านแม่ค้าน่ารัก ให้ชิม ให้โชว์ คุณอังกฤษได้บ้าง มีห้องน้ำอยู่ตลอดทาง
Ideal para hacer compras y comer ya que tiene muchos puestos de comida callejera

Lo mejor de Chengdu, una calle de estilo tradicional chino, llena de comida, souvenirs, bebidas, comercio en general. Puedes ver el espectáculo de máscaras y escuchar música en vivo mientras disfrutas de una rica comida y una cerveza bien fría. Definitivamente una parada obligada en la ciudad.
很典型的中國商業步行街，用三國時代的故事作歷史背景，有著各式各樣的手工藝品、紀念品和全國各步行街都會看見的一式一樣的小食餐廳，比較商業化。如果想嘗試正宗地道的當地代表性食物，還是建議到別的地方，如果只想試下大概味道的話，不妨一試。
古い町並みが残っている「錦里」。食べ物やお土産が軒先にずらりと並んで観光客をお出迎え。 午前中は比較的空いています。お昼ごろには人が増え続け観光どころではありません。 行くなら朝早くか、暖かい電球が魅力的な夜がお勧めです。最寄り駅は地下鉄３号線「高升橋駅」歩いて５～１０分になります。

商业气息蛮浓的一个地方，就在武侯祠的后门，说实在的，第一次去，还觉得蛮新鲜的，各种小吃，各种文艺青年的打卡地，小桥流水，茶馆、餐厅、川剧、掏耳朵，也兜售一些与所有风景点别无二致的、千篇一律的纪念品。去了几次，也就觉得很是一般。 小吃都是极其平常的小吃，和全国各地的景点小吃街没啥两样，唯一不同就是三大炮和兔头。茶馆呢，也是稀松平常的菜色，尚不如街边小餐馆的川菜。吃饭时间是没有川剧看的，说是要下午两点开始，结果两点半才开始，零零散散三两桌围坐着不多人，川剧打锣开场，短短几个数分钟就结束的小片段，与其说欣赏，不如说作为游客的猎奇，倒也符合现代人和游客的心态，最开心的莫过于邻桌的孩子，又蹦又跳，又吵又闹。倒是川剧的两个穆桂英女演员确实让人惊艳！另外，变脸演员走下戏台，在桌前表演，让我们有幸近距离欣赏，机会委实难得！滑稽戏的演员功底也是异常深厚，身段柔软令人惊叹！ 掏耳朵绝对不建议在这里尝试！几个小年青用工具装模作样掏几下，短短时间就了结，更像是仪式体验。 基本是建议去一次就够了！
雖然當地人認為錦里是針對觀光客而建的仿古街，毫無文化可言，但對於無暇深入探訪成都的觀光客來說，在知名景點武侯祠旁的錦里不失為一個相當理想的選擇。這裡有大部分成都的代表性小吃，儘管講究的吃貨覺得不夠道地，但熱鬧的各色店家足夠讓初訪客開心的吃吃逛逛了！
